title: A Study to Investigate the Safety, Tolerability, and Exposure of Single Doses of the study medicine STK-002, in Patients with Autosomal Dominant Optic Atrophy (ADOA)
official: Osprey: An Open-label Study to Investigate the Safety, Tolerability, and Exposure of Single Ascending Doses of the Antisense Oligonucleotide STK-002 in Patients with Autosomal Dominant Optic Atrophy
summary:
Main objective: • To evaluate the safety and tolerability of single ascending doses of STK 002 in patients with ADOA
• To determine the exposure in serum following single intravitreal (IVT) doses of STK-002
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. 1. Patient must be ≥18 to <55 years to participate in Part A and ≥6 to <18 years to participate in Part B
2. 2. Patient must have a clinical diagnosis of ADOA and have a heterozygous OPA1 gene variant confirmed at Screening by central lab genotyping
3. 3. Patient must have a BCVA EDTRS letter score of ≥35 and ≤70 in the intended eye, with the exception of the first two patients in Cohort 1 of Part A who must have a BCVA ETDRS letter score ≥5 and ≤35 in the intended eye
4. 4. Patient’s screening/baseline full field electroretinogram (ffERG) and optical coherence tomography (OCT) images are acceptable prior to dosing
Exclusion criteria:
1. 1. Patient has a gain-of-function variant, or compound heterozygous or homozygous pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant in the OPA1 gene
2. 2. Patient has extraocular phenotypic manifestations of (syndromic) ADOA (ADOA-plus) or have Behr syndrome
3. 3. Patient has, or has a history of, any ocular condition in the intended eye that, in the opinion of the Investigator, could affect study parameters
4. 4. Patient is considered to be at risk for uveitis or ocular infection during the study period
5. 5. Patient is taking, or has taken at any time, any medication or treatment that can or might cause an optic neuropathy
